title: Review of c48's nucleation-breaks-heredity negative on fresh seed 5 (trait arm and identical-stream twin, t=20000): the normal-turnover mutants never establish (at most 2 bodies), the trait arm runs down to one label-less body, the twin keeps 10 labelled bodies
summary: Labkit runs of the finding's world.py on seed 5, 192^2, 200 frames (t=20000): trait arm WORLD_P {b2 0.3, inoc_kind 2, swap_T 100, wash_T 1000} and the b2=0 twin with the same event streams. Per-kind counts from the rendered frames (kinds.py, c48's rule: the larger label if >= 0.5, else label-less). Trait arm (g1, g2, label-less) at t=3400/10100/16800/20000: (1,5,0)/(1,4,0)/(1,1,0)/(0,0,1); labkit 2 persistent splits, generation 2, 7 nucleations. Twin: (1,6,0)/(2,6,0)/(3,6,0)/(5,5,0); 10 persistent splits, generation 3, 6 nucleations. The trait arm's last labelled body shrinks away by t~19200 and a label-less condensate stands at t=20000 (rerun/seed5_trait/sheet.png).

observations.H: kinds_trait.json vs kinds_twin.json: mutants (g1) at most 2 bodies in the trait arm and gone by t=20000 while the population runs down to 1 label-less body; twin ends with 5 g1 and 5 g2

seeds_run.result: pass (run-down to extinction of labelled bodies, as on the finding's seed 1, with one label-less body at the end, as on seed 0)

controls_run.H: rerun/seed5_twin (b2=0, same seed, swap and washout streams)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and few bodies (at most 10). Labkit renders 120 of 201 frames, so counts are about every 100-200 t. Only one label-less body appears here, so the refill by nucleation is weaker than on the finding's seed 0, but the main result holds: the mutants do not spread and the trait arm loses its labelled population.
